facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling worsened in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September.

facts.heading: Hannah's teaching experience
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years and has loved it.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I've loved it.

facts.heading: Hannah's new role
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school, and the head asked her to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah worries that people picked the wrong person for her role and that someone will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety on Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah experiences chest tightness and rehearsing Monday's meetings on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question, her answers, and what others might think if she gets something wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah imagines people think she is out of her depth or that the job was given to a teacher who cannot read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Email rewriting for governors
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week, I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Email topic and fear
facts.content: The email was about the change to the behavior policy, and Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: Change to the behavior policy.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves's positive view
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, told Hannah in September he was delighted.
facts.evidence: that he told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of inauthenticity
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable, as if she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparison to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat, whose mother was a head teacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's career success
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a brilliant head teacher, and a library was named after her after she retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they have named a library after her.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother

facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive advice

facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Impact of mother's advice

facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.
